note: Every Claude Code fact v2 relies on (ARCHITECTURE §9). kind api: each `typings` fragment is in the typings snapshot (comments and whitespace aside), or, as {in, has}, each member is inside the declaration that starts at `in`. kind internal: undocumented, the binary holds each `search` string (ASCII: the binary keeps other text as UTF-16); at most 10 (PRD C2), each with its reason, its one fallback and the feature request it needs. feature: the SUB_HUMAN_CC_OFF value that turns its part off. checked: the versions the entry was checked on. Not an entry: §9's 'Managed machines' row, since v2 uses none of the hooks the guard skips, and the command hooks it leaves alone are command-hooks. npm run probe checks them all.

entries.surface: tool.call middleware after next(e); Edit and Write results carry filePath, Bash carries gitOperation; isError on a failed call
entries.note: Activity updates (R12) come from the results; bashEditDiff is @internal and not used.

entries.surface: TaskCreate result {task:{id,subject,description?}}, TaskUpdate result statusChange
typings: TaskCreate: { task: { id: string subject: string description?: string }
entries.note: The native task mirror (R23) reads the results, never the task files.

entries.surface: $.tool.list: whether this session has the Task tools
entries.note: Whether they are on is typed; why they are off is task-tool-gate.

entries.surface: prompt.submit hook context (100k characters an entry, 200k in all)
entries.note: Per-turn context (R15a). Not prompt.context, which fires once per conversation. It also fires for peer and plugin prompts.

entries.surface: $.session.append notes and tool.call result context, read inside a long tool loop
entries.note: The overlap heads-up (R15d) without starting a turn.

entries.surface: $.ui.status and $.ui.log (2,000 characters drawn)
entries.note: Who's here and the unread count under the prompt (R15b); debug lines.

entries.surface: $.ui.ask answered with a label or Other text; rejects when dismissed or in -p
typings: ask: (question: string, options?: readonly string[] | AskOptions) => Promise<string>;
entries.note: Let in / Refuse, keep / room / send, and the plan review card.

entries.surface: $.ui.open pane; pane bodies scroll (ui.scroll)
entries.note: The full plan, scrollable. An unasked pane only places from 144 columns, so it opens from the card.

entries.surface: tool.call on ExitPlanMode: result {plan, filePath?}
typings: ExitPlanMode: { plan: string | null isAgent: boolean filePath?: string
entries.note: Plan approval asks keep / room / send (R18); the rejection shape is not needed.

entries.surface: $.prompt.submit (runs once the session is idle), turn.complete isAborted to retry, session.stop, $.session.surfaces
entries.note: A wake (R10) is skipped when surfaces() is empty.

entries.surface: turn.start and turn.complete; the Notification command hook's notification_type
typings: hook_event_name: 'Notification'; message: string; title?: string; notification_type: string;
entries.note: Working or idle; waiting on a permission prompt is best-effort, about 6 s late.

entries.surface: session.repo {root, remote, name} and $.process.run(git) for the branch
typings: run: (argv: readonly string[], init?: ProcessRunInit) => Promise<ProcessRunResult>;
entries.note: session.repo has no branch; $.vcs is experimental and not used.

entries.surface: session.send hook at the sender, answered {isDelivered}
entries.note: Claude-to-Claude routing (R6) at the sender, because session.receive carries no sender.

entries.surface: sessionTitle from a SessionStart command hook
entries.note: NAME.CODE addressing; uniqueness is session-title-unique.

entries.surface: $.clock.every + $.fs.stat + $.fs.read of the room's tail file; crypto.subtle.digest
entries.note: There is no watch: polled every 0.5 to 1 s, 4 MiB a read; the hash chain is checked in the module.

entries.surface: $.tool.register + tool.run
entries.note: Claude's tools (share, read, plan, task) are the module's; there is no MCP server.

entries.surface: $.process.spawn and $.http.fetch to loopback
entries.note: The module has no Node and no import(); spawned children die with it, so a daemon detaches itself.

entries.surface: command hooks in hooks.json: UserPromptExpansion (the /sub-human command), SessionEnd
entries.note: Documented; they survive managed-machine policy, which can refuse the module.

entries.surface: the Task tools are off when CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS is false, and otherwise on only for some models and providers unless CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS is set
entries.reason: To tell the person in one line why their session has no Task tools and which launch env var turns them on (R23a).
entries.fallback: Say only that the native task tools are off here, without the why.
entries.request: Q12: a plugin-declared opt-in for the Task tools (not yet filed).
entries.note: $.tool.list says whether they are on (tool-list).

entries.surface: a plugin's $.prompt.submit between turns enters framed as '<plugin> plugin sent a message:'
search: This is how Claude Code surfaces a prompt a plugin submits between
entries.reason: The wake's own text (bob's Claude asks: ...) is written to read right inside that frame.
entries.fallback: No wakes: the message waits in the status line and the next turn's context.
entries.request: Document the frame a plugin prompt gets (not yet filed).
entries.note: It shows as a prompt from the plugin.

entries.surface: a session.send hook's {isDelivered: true} without next is honoured: the message is not sent on, and the sender's tool reports it delivered
search: Delivered by a plugin hook; nothing else was sent.
entries.reason: Claude-to-Claude messages to NAME.CODE go over the room channel, not Claude Code's own delivery.
entries.fallback: No Claude-to-Claude messages to members on other machines.
entries.request: Type {isDelivered: true} without next as the hook's own delivery (not yet filed).
entries.note: The engine's tool result when a hook delivered it; U6 showed it honoured on 2.1.330. ARCHITECTURE §9: possibly internal.

entries.surface: a sessionTitle already held by a live session is not given to a second one (tengu_session_name_uniqueness, on by default)
entries.reason: NAME.CODE must name one session, or a message could reach the wrong one.
entries.note: The second session yields and keeps a suffixed name.
